slides.title: Your Team View shows every function and its owner in one place.
slides.headline: Your Team View shows every function and its owner in one place.
notes: The Team View shows each function, the person who volunteered to own it, and their title. It is all in one view.
When one person owns two functions, it shows in red: a load to watch. Planned functions show where people can grow.
Show it to the whole team at a town hall whenever it changes.

artwork.alt: The Team View for the example subscription company, matching the Function Chart’s agreed owners. Head of Company: Pat, CEO. Below: Marketing, Chris; Sales, Andrew; Operations, Jen; Development, Jen; Finance, Allison; People, Pat. Pat and Jen each own two functions, so their cards are red. A dashed, planned Customer Success function sits below Sales, for next year.

slides.title: Does every function have a critical number?
slides.headline: Does every function have a critical number?
notes: Open the Team View in Metronome on the screen. Fix any difference from the chart now.
Each owner says their critical number out loud. It is the number they look at every day.
slides.support: Check the Team View in Metronome against your chart.
body: Every function on the chart is in the Team View, with its owner.
Each owner names one critical number for the function.
The number can be financial or not. Listen for widgets.

slides.title: Every function owner has a scorecard, reviewed every 90 days.
slides.headline: Every function owner has a scorecard, reviewed every 90 days.

artwork.alt: A team member and their team lead sit at a table with one scorecard between them, each speaking in turn.

body: What: one page per function, saying what success looks like.
Why: everyone knows what they own and how we measure it.
How often: every 90 days, scored 0, 1 or 2.
Who: the owner, then their team lead. Then they compare.
notes: The scores: 0 below, 1 meets, 2 exceeds. The owner scores first, then their team lead, then they talk about the differences.
A scorecard is not a job description or a list of priorities. It belongs to a function on the KFFM.
The review is a two-way conversation. The learning is where the two scores differ. At the end, the team member gives their leader feedback.
First time, keep it to the team member and their team lead. Metronome runs the reviews.

slides.title: A scorecard says what success looks like in a function.
slides.headline: A scorecard says what success looks like in a function.
notes: Purpose in one sentence. Three to five functional accountabilities, each starting Owns, including execution. Exactly two metrics: one widget the owner controls and one fiscal metric the role owns. Six to eight key competencies. The company’s core values.
Scorecards live in Metronome. The homework starts with the Head of Company scorecard, shared with the team.

artwork.alt: An example Operations scorecard for the subscription company, owned by Jen, laid out as Metronome lays out a scorecard. Purpose: turn every new subscription into an active customer, fast. Core Values: your company’s core values, in this role. Functional Accountabilities: four, each starting with Owns. Key Competencies: six. Metrics Owned by the Function: activated subscriptions a week, and cost per activation.
